subject: Dedicated pool — GPU selection, pricing options, and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Lia Patel <lia.patel@nebulahealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03 09:12 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity questions — baseline ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: Nebula Health is evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool to serve a combination of two workloads — a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) customer QA flow (short context windows, high QPS) and an internal clinical model for long-context summarization (large context, memory-heavy). We need predictable throughput and a pricing anchor for a 12-month reserved commit.

Can you send:
- A clear breakdown (perf/$) for A100 vs H100 vs L40S across those two workload profiles, including memory considerations (40GB vs 80GB).
- Recommended pool sizing to meet a target of 12k QPS for the RAG path at p95 latency <= 200ms for short completions, and a baseline of 50 concurrent long-context summarizations (up to 128k tokens) with acceptable tail latency.
- Suggested reserved commit tiers, what discount bands apply, and whether we can mix GPU types in a single pool with fallback routing.
- Any SLA/throughput guarantees you can commit to at each tier.

We're prepared to commit to a 12-month contract if the math and SLAs align. Looking for a call next week to walk through.

Best,
Lia Patel
Procurement Lead, Nebula Health
procurement@nebulahealth.com

---

Note: we may share additional perf traces after the call.
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Lia Patel <lia.patel@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity questions — baseline ask

Hi Lia — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise, pragmatic breakdown and our recommended path forward. I attached a formal quote and a pool-sizing worksheet for your team to tweak.

TL;DR recommendations
- Mix-of-pools: Start with an H100-dominant pool for RAG throughput and a small L40S subpool for non-critical batch inference. Use A100 (80GB) instances for long-context summarization nodes. Use smart routing to pin long jobs to A100s.
- Commit: 12-month reserved commit covering 60% of baseline expected throughput gives best price predictability. We can scale with burst capacity at defined premium.
- Discounting: sliding scale — 10% for 6-month, 18% for 12-month, 24%+ for 24-month multi-region commits (negotiable).

Perf/$ notes (ballpark, per model-family normalized to tokens/sec per GPU-dollar):
- H100 (80GB): best for high-throughput transformer models (decoder-only and many instruction-tuned models). Perf/$: highest at batch-friendly workloads; for short RAG completions expect ~1.0x baseline perf/$.
- A100 (80GB): better when you need large KV cache and long contexts — for very long summarization jobs it's ~1.1x perf for memory-heavy ops vs H100, but lower raw throughput per GPU on short requests.
- L40S (48GB): cost-effective for inference where memory and p95 latency at scale aren't critical — typically 0.6–0.8x perf/$ vs H100 but 30–40% cheaper per GPU-hour.

Sizing suggestions to meet your stated targets (start-of-deal baseline):
- RAG (12k QPS target, short 256-token completions, p95 <=200ms): estimate H100 pool of 8–10 cards with continuous batching and prefix caching, plus autoscale up to 14 for peaks. We can provide concrete bench numbers with your model binary.
- Long-context summarization (50 concurrent up to 128k tokens): 4x A100-80GB or 3x H100-80GB configured with large KV caches and pinned allocations. A100 gives safer memory headroom for 128k contexts.

Throughput guarantees / SLA constructs
- We offer committed throughput expressed as tokens/sec per pool and a p95 latency SLO for the RAG path. For 12-month commit at the 60% baseline tier we can include a financial credit if monthly throughput drops below 90% of committed tokens/sec for that tier. Exact credit schedule in attached quote.

Pricing structure (examples)
- Option A (H100-heavy): commit to 10 H100 equiv GPUs (12-mo): list price $Xk/month, 18% discount applied — includes 24 hours/month free burst and 99.5% uptime SLA.
- Option B (Hybrid A100+H100): commit to 6 H100 + 4 A100 (12-mo): list price $Yk/month, 20% discount for mixed pool; A100 skew increases the per-month price but improves memory headroom.
- Option C (Cost-first L40S mix): commit to 12 L40S (12-mo): list price $Zk/month, 22% discount — lower unit cost, higher risk on p95 for tight latency targets.

Operational tradeoffs to call out
- Memory: A100 80GB nodes reduce the need for sharding and complex KV stitching for 128k contexts. If you plan many concurrent 128k jobs, A100s avoid engineering tradeoffs.
- Tail latency: H100 + aggressive batching gives better aggregate perf and perf/$ for short requests, but p95 can worsen if not carefully tuned. We use continuous batching + adaptive priority routing to meet p95 SLOs.
- Mixed pools: fully supported. We recommend routing rules that pin long-context jobs to A100s and use H100 for RAG. Fallback rules can route to a lower-cost L40S pool when capacity constrained (with degraded SLOs).

Next steps
1) If helpful I can run a 2-hour bench with your model(s) to produce exact perf/$ numbers.
2) We can align on a 12-month commitment band (percentage of baseline) and I’ll send a redline-friendly contract with the SLA/credit table.
3) Schedule a call — I have availability Tue/Thu next week.

Attachments: formal quote + sizing sheet. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9812345

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the math.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

Priyom — quick internal note before we push the quote. Two negotiation levers we can flex without escalating to legal:
- Commit length and discount: push for 18% on 12-mo as baseline, but we can go to 20% if they agree to a 70% utilization commitment (measured monthly).
- Free burst: offer 48 hours of free burst in the first month instead of 24, but tie it to a 30-day ramp plan documented in the MSA.
- SLA credits: keep the 90% throughput floor for crediting, but make credits capped at 30% of monthly fee.

Also suggest we include a simple 1-page comparison grid in the next email that shows: p95 latency expected, memory headroom, perf/$ qualitative score, and recommended primary workload for each GPU type. Keeps procurement focused.

If Lia asks about p95 measurement — assume we state p95 measured under steady-state with continuous batching and 95th-percentile request size from their telemetry; we'll need their sample traces to finalize.

If you want, I can take the pricing conversation on the next sync — I can offer a verbal 20% if they sign within 10 business days.

—Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — the detail is helpful. A few follow-ups before we lock time:

1) Can you provide the perf/$ numbers in a tiny table (H100 vs A100 vs L40S) for: short RAG requests (256 tokens) and long summarizations (128k tokens)? Please show the assumptions (batch size, p95 vs p50, tokens/sec measurement).
2) For the SLA/throughput credit, is the 90% floor applied at pool level monthly or per-route (RAG vs summarization)? We need guarantees per route.
3) Confirm whether the mixed-pool routing and the A100 pinning are included in the managed price or if there’s an additional ops surcharge.

We can do a 30-min call Wed 10/07 at 11am PT to review the quote — invite sent. Also please share the pool-sizing-sheet.xlsx in editable form (not PDF).

Lia Patel
